title: Field theories and critical excitations at anyon condensation transitions
abstract: Anyon condensation transitions remain challenging to characterize especially when the condensing anyons are non-abelian. We develop two complementary approaches for extracting information about the transition from the categorical data of the parent topological order and the condensate. The first adapts a Ginzburg-Landau procedure developed for $1+1$D transitions in the SymTFT setting to $2+1$D anyon condensation transitions. The construction applies when the anyons participating in the condensate have integer quantum dimensions. The second gives a criterion for identifying which point and loop excitations become critical at a continuous transition. The key step is to determine which anyon loops remain condensed throughout. All other loops become critical, while a point excitation becomes critical if it braids trivially with every condensed loop. We illustrate both proposals in several abelian and non-abelian examples.
summary: This paper develops advanced field-theoretic tools to characterize anyon condensation transitions in 2+1D topological systems, especially when non-abelian anyons are involved. It proposes adapting the Ginzburg-Landau framework and provides a diagnostic criterion based on the criticality of topological excitations. This work advances the mathematical understanding of how topological order dictates the nature of quantum phase transitions.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize anyon condensation transitions, particularly in the challenging case where the condensing anyons are non-abelian.
main_result: It develops two complementary theoretical approaches: adapting a Ginzburg-Landau procedure for 2+1D transitions and establishing a criterion to identify critical point and loop excitations.
method: The methods involve deriving effective Lagrangian terms from the categorical data of the parent topological order using fusion trees, and analyzing the gap closing of excitations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2+1 dimensional topological phases characterized by anyonic excitations, modeling transitions driven by the condensation of these anyons (e.g., in systems related to $Z_2$ or $S_3$ symmetries).
key_observables: The form of the effective Lagrangian ($L$), the nature of critical point/loop excitations, and the universality class of the transition (e.g., Ising universality class).
important_parameters: The quantum dimensions of the condensing anyons, and the dimensionality (2+1D) of the system.
main_assumptions: The Ginzburg-Landau procedure is assumed applicable when condensing anyons have integer quantum dimensions; the analysis often assumes the transition is driven by the condensation of a specific subset of anyons.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates order two and order three fusion trees of condensing anyons fusing into the trivial anyon 1.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the general problem, then detailing the Ginzburg-Landau adaptation for 2+1D, followed by the criterion for identifying critical excitations, and illustrating these proposals with several abelian and non-abelian examples.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between topological order (a core concept in condensed matter theory) and continuum field theory descriptions of phase transitions is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum states in AMO systems.
